$$

$$

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{1}$ is 
${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=2\text{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2\text{i}t}.
$$

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2\text{i}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))+\text{i}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}] \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
